title: Blackwater Cyber: Preliminary Backup Status, 15:38 CT

fields.subject: PRELIMINARY – Backup status, 15:38 CT
fields.body:
Anil,

This is a preliminary update. All of it may change as we learn more.

1) The last MES backup we can call clean is the Wednesday, March 24, 07:05 CT snapshot. That is 31 hours before encryption, and your RPO is 15 minutes. Every snapshot after it contains .ironmelt artifacts.

2) The Dubuque MES replica (ICM-MES-DBQ-01) is partly encrypted. Three of its seven database volumes are affected.

3) No backup or replica is cleared for restore. We will not clear any of them until we finish the persistence sweep, which we expect to take 12 to 18 hours.

4) We are reviewing about 940 GB of outbound traffic that went to a hosting provider on Tuesday night. We have not yet tied it to the 1.2 TB claim in the ransom note.

We recommend that this engagement run through outside counsel from here on. Please confirm, and we will route future reports to counsel.

Mara
fields.signature:
Mara Lindqvist, GCFA
Lead Examiner, Incident Response
Blackwater Cyber
Mobile 555-0143 | IR hotline 555-0144

instructorNote: This email tells the CISO and GC that the backups are 31 hours old, against a 15-minute RPO, and that none is cleared for restore. Watch for these steps: the CISO orders no restores and rebuilds instead of cleaning (IBIARO 4). The GC records when the CISO notified her, against the 15:05 deadline, and sets the Disclosure Committee for 19:00 at the latest. She moves Blackwater under Harrow Fenn LLP for privilege. The 940 GB transfer should be logged as an open question, not a conclusion.
